title: Evaluate ModelAttentionBackend (comfy kitchen attention) as the built-in answer to the four Sage rejections
description: ComfyUI core added a ModelAttentionBackend node with a 'comfy kitchen attention' mode. It is NOT faster than SageAttention - it is almost as fast - but for Vision that is the wrong axis. Vision has rejected Sage four separate times, never on speed: MPI-50 (local engine never installs it), MPI-189 (source build unreliable on cu130 in GPU-less Docker, so the product Pod ships the SDPA fallback), MPI-145 (--use-sage-attention crashes LTX-2.3 on Ada sm_89 with a CUDA unspecified launch failure, gated via SAGE_DISABLED_ARCHS), and the Windows JIT tax (~2x SLOWER on embedded py3.13, which ships no compiler). A backend built into core has none of those costs: no wheel, no nvcc, no arch gating, one node in a graph. So 'almost as fast as Sage, installs everywhere' beats 'faster than Sage on Blackwell Pods only', which is all Vision ever had. BLOCKED on the engine bump: verified 2026-08-22 that ModelAttentionBackend is absent from comfy/ and comfy_extras/ in v0.31.0 - the tag pinned in dev_configs/node_lock.json and the version on the G:/ComfyUi bench. Unblocks when core moves past 0.31.0. Third point, and it softens the one objection that could kill this: most Vision models ship INT8 already, so the 'approximate attention loses precision' argument (the stated reason docs/models/h3/performance.md rejected MiniMaxH3MemoryEfficientSageAttentionPatch) lands much softer on a stack whose weights are already int8. Measure it per model rather than treating 'it is approximate' as a finished rejection.
